tool_input.message:
F5 is fixed. Since the mission had already closed when the F5 addendum arrived, I filed a factual correction rather than reopening a round: `ethos mission correct m-2026-10-21-001 --file .tmp/missions/results/fc6o-f5-correction.yaml` → recorded.

Two new commits on fix/push-guard-worktree, both passing `make check`:

1. `c30795a` fix(hooks): resolve push-guard branch where the push invocation runs, not just payload cwd
2. `bb3c91b` docs(changelog): record the F5 branch-resolution fix

Full commit list for this mission (6 total): `0f3bd1d`, `f3dd113`, `cad79b2`, `cc26d0d`, `58c873b`, `7b73424`, `c30795a`, `bb3c91b` — 8 commits actually, across the hook fix, its test, the Makefile wiring, and three CHANGELOG updates.

F5 probe results, all against `c30795a`:

- **(a)** `git -C <main-checkout> push` from feature-worktree cwd: DENIED (was allowed before the fix).
- **(b)** `git -C <feature-worktree> push origin feat/example` from main-checkout cwd: ALLOWED, confirming no over-deny.
- **(c)** `cd <main-checkout> && git push` from feature-worktree cwd: DENIED.
- **(d)** payload cwd pointing at a non-repo directory, plain push: DENIED, fail closed.
- **(e)** detached HEAD in the temp repo, plain push: DENIED, fail closed.

Implementation: the branch check now resolves its scope from the push invocation's own text — the last `-C <dir>` global flag (git's own semantics: each `-C` is relative to the previous one, so only the cumulative last matters) or, failing that, the last `cd <dir>` seen in command position before the invocation — falling back to the payload's `cwd` only when neither is present. Both the command-position and destination-ref regexes are extended to recognize `-C <dir>`, since a `-C`-redirected invocation was previously invisible to classification entirely, not just to the branch check. The branch check fails closed: an unenterable directory or an empty `git branch --show-current` (no repo, or detached HEAD) now denies with a stated reason instead of falling through to allow.

Per your explicit instruction, ordinary `cd`-containing compound commands with no `git push` anywhere are untouched — the cd-scanning logic only runs after the command-position check has already confirmed a real push invocation is present.

Test suite grew from 30 to 40 cases (five new scenarios × jq/no-jq). One subtlety worth flagging: the non-repository test fixture had to be built with `env -u TMPDIR mktemp -d` rather than a plain subdirectory of the shared work directory — TMPDIR for this whole suite is this repo's own `.tmp/`, so an ordinary subdirectory still sits inside this checkout's working tree and `git branch --show-current` would silently walk past it to this repo's own branch, defeating the fail-closed case it's meant to exercise. All 40 cases pass, shellcheck clean on both scripts, `make check` clean on both commits (full logs read, not truncated).

`git status` is clean on everything in my write set. Pre-existing out-of-scope diffs (`.claude/agents/kwb.md`, `.punt-labs/vox/vox.md`, three untracked agent files, one empty ethos lock file) are untouched.
